_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: God planted a vineyard and looked for good fruit.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved.
The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This is the Lord's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.
We are the vine, planted and tended and called to bear fruit.
Turn again, O God; look down and tend this vine.
Come, let us worship the God who will not give us up.
We come to the keeper of the vineyard. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Walk into the vineyard at evening, the rows heavy and green, planted by a God who cleared the ground and waited long for the fruit.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
We are that vine, brought out of Egypt and planted, and we have not always borne what God hoped.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
Yet the stone we rejected God has made the cornerstone, and on it he is building something we did not expect.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
Turn again, look down from heaven, tend this vine your right hand planted.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
So come into the vineyard of grace and worship.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: God planted a vineyard and waited for good fruit.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
The stone we rejected has become the cornerstone.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
Tend this vine your own right hand has planted.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
Come, let us worship the keeper of the vineyard.
We come to bear fruit. Amen.
